item.research_question: How does varying Nb content (x = 0.3, 0.4, 0.5) and subsequent annealing at 1000 °C affect the microstructure, hardness, and friction/wear properties of AlCrTiVNbx high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting using pure metals (>99.9 wt%) melted 5 times; annealing at 1000 °C for 2 h with a heating speed of 10 °C/min followed by furnace cooling to room temperature
item.test_conditions: Room temperature, reciprocating mode, GCr15 stainless-steel ball (φ5 mm), normal load 5 N, oscillating amplitude 5 mm, frequency 2 Hz, sliding time 30 min
key_findings: Annealing transformed the single-phase BCC structure of the as-cast alloys into multi-phase structures containing BCC, HCP, and FCC phases.
The hardness of the Nb0.5 alloy increased from 543 HV in the casting state to 725 HV after annealing.
The average friction coefficient of the annealed Nb0.5 alloy was 0.154, significantly lower than the as-cast value of 0.333.
The annealed Nb0.5 alloy exhibited the lowest wear rate of 2.117 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m), representing a 62.9% improvement over the as-cast state.
The content of the FCC phase and HCP phase increased with the increase in Nb content after annealing.
The as-cast alloys showed a single BCC phase, while annealed Nb0.3 showed a BCC/HCP duplex structure and Nb0.4/Nb0.5 showed a BCC/HCP/FCC three-phase structure.
The wear mechanism for all samples included abrasive wear, adhesive wear, and oxidative wear.
item.mechanism: The improvement in wear resistance is attributed to precipitation strengthening caused by the increase in NbCrAl precipitated phases and the lubrication effect provided by the FCC phase (Al11V) which has good plasticity.
quotes: The hardness value of the annealed HEAs is greatly enhanced compared with the casting state, and the hardness of the Nb0.5 HEA is increased from 543 HV to 725 HV after annealing.
We believe that the precipitation strengthening after the annealing treatment and the lubrication effect of the FCC phase are the reasons for the significant improvement in wear resistance.

The wear rate is 2.117 × 10−5 mm3/(N·m). This is because the FCC phase and HCP phase produced by amplitude modulation decomposition after the annealing treatment play a role in precipitation strengthening, and the FCC phase has good plasticity and plays a certain role in self-lubrication.
